simple.meaning: שָׂקַר (sâqar) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to ogle , i.e. blink coquettishly.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Isaiah, beginning at Isaiah 3:16. The surrounding contexts include family line.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שָׂקַר (H8265) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: שָׂקַר (sâqar) / H8265 is traced through Isaiah 3:16 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H8265. saqar [ שָׂקַר ] verb Pi`el ogle (Aramaic סְקַר look at ( ᵑ7 Job 20:9 ; 28:7 ), סַקְרָנִית looking about, ogling ; eye with envy or hatred (e.g. 1Sam 18:9 ᵑ6 ); compare De Is ); — Participle feminine plural עֵינַיִם מְשַׂקְּרוֺת Isa 3:16 ogling of eyes (women of Jerusalem). שַׂר see שׂרר .
